carbon_policy_signal.item: EU methane emissions reporting for fossil fuels delayed by Trump-administration lobbying; COP31 fossil phase-out collapse weakens global climate consensus and long-term EU ETS enforcement urgency.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Delay reduces near-term regulatory pressure on fossil-fuel operators to invest in abatement and fuel-switching; weakens medium-term demand for carbon allowances and power-generation decarbonization, capping EUA upside and supporting thermal-dispatch margins.

freshness_caveat: Coal (333 days stale, as_of 2025-12-26) and Clean Dark spread (328 days stale, as_of 2025-12-31) undermine thermal merit-order and fuel-switch signals; thermal stack assessment requires urgent data refresh. All other metrics current as of 2026-11-23–24.
risk_flags: Coal data 333 days old (as of 2025-12-26); Clean Dark stale since 2025-12-31 — thermal spread signals unreliable until fresh data surfaces.

EU storage 68.41% (17.7pp below seasonal) + renewable share 29.51% (18th-percentile) = tight winter gas call; refill pace failure through Dec will force sustained high thermal capacity-factor.

COP31 fossil-phase-out collapse + methane-reporting delay (Trump lobby) structurally reduce EU decarbonization urgency, capping long-dated carbon and power upside via weakened policy enforcement signal.

base.summary: Storage deficit sustains 70+ TTF and 80–95th-percentile power; renewables remain depressed; coal cheap but merit-order opaque pending data refresh.

downside.summary: Mild weather + wind recovery lift renewable share to 40th-pctile; US LNG export surge to Europe floods arbitrage window; storage refill catches up to seasonal.

upside.summary: Cold front + wind drought extend renewable deficit into Dec; storage drain accelerates to 1pp/day; thermal runs hard, TTF rallies into supply-tight regime.

top_takeaway: GB power 92nd-percentile amid storage deficit 17.7pp below seasonal; coal at 8th-percentile signals tight thermal economics and fuel-switch regime despite stale coal data.
